Welcome

One semester
at Baoshan

You are here for a semester at SHU (Baoshan Campus), hosted by UTSEUS — the Sino-European School of Technology of Shanghai University. This guide is not about courses or credits: it is about everything else.

The campus sits in the north of Shanghai, about 40 minutes from the centre on metro Line 7. It is a large, self-contained place: six canteens, a swimming pool, two libraries and a clinic, all within the gates. Step outside and you find cheap restaurants, phone shops, banks, supermarkets and a Sam's Club — enough to live comfortably without going downtown, which is a metro ride away rather than a walk.

Keep this on your phone. Chinese names are given throughout: paste them into Gaode Maps (高德) or Dianping (大众点评) to find your way. In the online version, the « → open in maps » button next to an address opens it straight in Gaode, and every pin on the maps is clickable.

This guide complements the survival guide made by AFEC — but it is specifically for you: students coming to UTSEUS for an exchange semester at SHU's Baoshan campus. For everything that applies anywhere in China (visas, VPN, apps, insurance, health, safety, culture), open the AFEC guide instead. Don't have it yet? Scan the code.

Arrival
Chapter II

Getting
to campus

You land a few days before term starts — use them well: almost everything that matters can be sorted before your first class. General formalities (visa, arrival card, VPN, insurance) are in the AFEC guide; this is the Baoshan-side plan.

1 · Reaching the campus

Take a Didi. After ten hours of flying, with a suitcase and a backpack, the metro is a rough first experience: a line change with luggage, stairs and rush-hour crowds. A Didi takes you door to door for at most 230 RMB from Pudong (1 h 15 to 1 h 30) or at most 120 RMB from Hongqiao (about 45 minutes). You will probably land alone rather than as a group — but if someone from your intake arrives around the same time, share the car.

If you'd rather take the metro (7–9 RMB), the principle is the same from both airports — Line 2 as far as Jing'an Temple, then Line 7 north — but the two airports sit at opposite ends of Line 2, so you ride in opposite directions:

  • From Pudong airport (PVG), the eastern end of the line — take Line 2 westbound at Pudong International Airport 浦东国际机场 and stay on it all the way to Jing'an Temple 静安寺 (no train change on the way), then Line 7 north to Shanghai University 上海大学. About 1 h 45.
  • From Hongqiao airport (SHA), the western end — take Line 2 eastbound at Hongqiao Airport T2 虹桥2号航站楼 to Jing'an Temple, then Line 7 north to Shanghai University. About 1 h 15.
UTSEUS · Baoshan Handbook04
Arrival
Chapter II · continued

Your first
few days

2 · First: a hotel next to campus

Book a few nights as close to campus as possible (search « 上海大学宝山校区 » on Trip.com) for the days before term starts: everything on your list — SIM, bank, getting your bearings — is then within walking distance. Most hotels register you with the police themselves — but not all of them do, so ask for the registration slip (临时住宿登记单) at reception and check you have it before you leave.

3 · Then your flat, with UTSEUS

You will be renting an apartment around the campus, and the school helps you find one — flats, agencies, contracts and flatmates go through Kay and Anicet, so ask them before signing anything.

Then register with the police — this one is on you. Every foreigner in China has to be declared at the address where they actually sleep; the slip you get is the official proof of where you live, and the bank, the university and your visa all ask for it. Once you move in, you have 24 hours to register at the local police station or online here — the new slip replaces the hotel one.

4 · Use those first days

In this order: SIM card (the SIM chapter — the bank needs a Chinese number, while the SIM only needs your passport), then a bank account (the bank chapter). After that, go and explore the campus and the streets around it with the maps on pages 6 and 7: find the west gate food street, your nearest canteen, the metro exits and the supermarket. Everything worth knowing is walking or cycling distance, so this is also the week to get comfortable with Alipay, the shared bikes and Dianping, without coursework on top.

5 · Registration, once term starts

Registration at SHU only happens when term begins — and you do not have to work it out on your own. Charly organises the whole thing: paperwork, the order it happens in, where to be and when. Just bring your documents and follow his instructions. The campus card 一卡通 — it pays the canteens and gets you through the gates — is handled the same way; once it is in your hand, everything you can do with it is in the campus-card chapter.

UTSEUS tip: photograph every document as you get it — passport page, visa, registration slip, admission letter, student card. You will be asked for them far more often than you expect, and a photo on your phone has settled many a counter conversation. And get yourself into the two WeChat groups (Chapter I) the day you arrive.

Chapter V

Campus card
& calendar

Topping up the campus card 一卡通

The card pays the canteens, gets you onto campus and covers the paid services inside it (showers, printing, pool tickets). Four ways to top it up:

With Alipay — the easiest, if you have a Chinese card
Search 支付宝校园卡 → add a card → « Shanghai University » → student number and name. Credited in minutes. Two catches: it needs a Chinese bank card (a foreign card linked to Alipay will not do), and the name must match your student card exactly.
With WeChat — on the campus network
Official account 上海大学信息门户 → 校内用户 → Smart Portal 智慧门户 → log in → 账户充值. Only works on the campus network, so do it from campus Wi-Fi.
With SHU WeCom 企业微信 to be confirmed
Install WeCom, domain shuedu, log in → Workspace → Life Services → 校园卡一卡通.
In cash
At the Yixin canteen 益新食堂, a staffed counter on the left of the left-hand entrance takes your card and your cash and loads it. It is the only place on campus that takes cash, and the only route that needs no Chinese bank card at all.

Autumn semester 2026

The semester opens on Friday 4 September with the opening ceremony; classes start on Monday 7 September · semester ends Sunday 10 January 2027.
Two public holidays fall inside it: Mid-Autumn on 25 September and Golden Week from 1 to 7 October — the whole country travels then, so book early or stay put.

Chapter V · continued

Your SHU account
& the campus Wi-Fi

One password unlocks both. You can only set it once you have your student card — the form asks for the number printed on it.

1 · Set your password

Go to newsso.shu.edu.cn and click Self-Activation. The form asks for four things:

Field on the formWhat to type
Student/Staff IDyour student number, printed on your student card
Full Nameexactly as written on the card
ID Numberyour passport number
Passwordone you choose — this is the password you are creating

The next page asks you to link a phone number, and it has to be a Chinese one — a foreign number will not be accepted. Get your SIM first (the SIM chapter).

Two more things worth knowing

  • Lost or demagnetised campus card: self-service reissue machines under building D, on the 6th floor of building A and in the one-stop service hall. Anything else: the info desk on the ground floor of building D.
  • The charity house 公益爱心屋: in the underground passage between buildings B and C — borrow clothes, buy basics, or just sit and read.
2 · Get on the campus Wi-Fi

Two networks, and the difference matters:

  • SHUWlan-1X — the one to use. Username: your student number, password: the one you just set. Connect once and your phone and laptop stay on it; you never log in again.
  • SHU (For all) — the fallback if SHUWlan-1X refuses you. It works, but it drops you every so often and makes you sign in again, so treat it as the spare.

Campus
Chapter VI

The campus
clinic

The campus clinic 校医院

Health centre, north gate 校医院→ open in maps
North gate 北门, next to the medical school · just inside the campus from the metro
Your first stop when something goes wrong — and a mandatory one if you want to be reimbursed. General medicine and surgery, dentistry, Chinese medicine, ENT and ophthalmology, gynaecology, dermatology, plus a lab, ultrasound, ECG and radiology on site.
Opening hours: published every Monday on the 上海大学学生会 WeChat account — slots vary by department.
Getting reimbursed: the 转诊单 rule

See a doctor at the campus clinic first; if needed they issue a referral slip (转诊单) for a designated hospital — Huashan North, Tongji, Shanghai Tenth or Sixth People’s.

Reimbursement: above a 300 RMB annual deductible — 70/60/50 % by hospital tier. A slip lasts one week and covers one visit to one department. Exceptions: emergencies and the holidays.

Chapter VI · continued

The two
libraries

Both open 8:00–22:00 during term, both entered with your campus card, and a book borrowed in one can go back to any of the three SHU libraries.

Main library 校本部图书馆

East of the Yixin canteen, facing the sunken plaza · close to the teaching buildings
Eight floors, humanities on 3–4 and 7, natural sciences on 6–7, with study desks on every floor and power sockets along the corridors. Two things matter: the 24-hour study space on the ground floor and the bookable study rooms 研习空间. Self-service printing on floors 5 and 8, main desk on floor 2.
Booking the 24-hour space to be confirmed: WeCom 企业微信 → Workspace → 24小时自修区预约, then pick area, seat and time. It only works on the campus network, so book it while you are on campus.
The service desk lends umbrellas 爱心伞 — free, on the second floor. Remember it the first time a Shanghai downpour catches you between buildings.

Qian Weichang library 钱伟长图书馆UTSEUS side

East zone, across from your building · the round one
Library, museum and university history hall in one spiral: floors 1–2 the SHU museum, 3 the Qian Weichang memorial, 3–4 the open stacks, 5 special collections, 6 discussion rooms, 7 reading space. Over 800 seats, face-recognition entry, self-service borrowing and printing.
Seats are booked, not taken to be confirmed: the day's system opens at 7:00 in WeCom → Workspace → 图书馆座位预约. Once there you must 签到 check in, 暂离 if you step out and 退座 when you leave — skip those and you collect a no-show against your name.

Shopping
on campus

Walk in through the west gate and the first thing you meet is a short commercial strip — the campus high street, and the answer to most small daily needs without leaving the grounds.

Education supermarket 上海教育超市 Shànghǎi jiàoyù chāoshì→ open in maps
Opposite the west gate basketball court
The everyday bazaar: toiletries, snacks, cleaning things. Next door, M&G 晨光文具 Chénguāng wénjù for notebooks and pens; hidden at the back, a second-hand bookshop where you can buy — and sell back — your books. Campus card, WeChat or Alipay.
Coffee & bubble tea→ open in maps
Luckin 瑞幸咖啡 Ruìxìng kāfēi — order in the app, collect in two minutes, a third of what Starbucks charges. Mixue 蜜雪冰城 Mìxuě bīngchéng for 4–10 RMB bubble tea, 芯茶 Xīn chá next door, and a bakery for the 8 a.m. emergency.
The rest of the strip
The fruit stand 尚大果品 Shàngdà guǒpǐn, where apples or seasonal mangoes cost a few yuan a jin. 加宋图文 Jiāsòng túwén for printing and binding, 8:00–22:00. And an optician 佳视眼镜 Jiāshì yǎnjìng — genuinely useful if you break your glasses two weeks in.
Elsewhere on campus
A convenience store 飞牛便利 Fēiniú biànlì in the east zone near UTSEUS, and in the south residences a 7-Eleven with a fruit shop and their own Luckin. Starbucks sits just outside the west gate if you want somewhere to sit down.
Inside the canteens
Yixin, Shuixiu, Wuxin and Liuyun each have a small shop on the ground floor — drinks, snacks, the thing you forgot between two classes.
Shops here turn over from year to year — this is what the campus maps show at the time of writing.

Fitness
Chapter VII

Sport &
gyms

A pleasant surprise: Baoshan is one of the best-equipped campuses in Shanghai — and Line 7 is your sports corridor for everything else. Almost everything is booked through WeChat mini-programs, so sort out your SIM first.

The gymnasium 体育馆

North of campus, near the east gatecampus card
Attached to the pool and the training hall · facing the Weichang building
A 4,200-seat arena whose floor is the campus's sports engine: 15 badminton courts with 15 nets — the number-one booking on campus, so reserve a day or two ahead through the SHU system in WeChat. Basketball, volleyball and floor hockey share the ground floor. Upstairs: fencing on the north side of floor 2, taekwondo on the south side over blue mats. Rooms T101, T115 and T145 are the gymnastics studios — pilates, yoga, dance.

The training hall 训练馆

Next door to the gymnasium
Room X101 is the table-tennis hall: 32 tables, and one of the most popular places on campus outside class hours — turn up and someone will play. Rooms X106 and X107, inside it, are dance studios with mirrored walls.

The pool 游泳馆

Between the gymnasium and the athletics track10–25 RMB
Two pools, and the distinction matters: the small pool is normally closed to students (training courses only). You swim in the big pool, which has a 1.2 m shallow half open to everyone and a 2 m deep half reserved for classes, the swim team and coach-supervised sessions. Free swimming always happens in the shallow half, and beginners are asked to stay out of the deep end. Swim caps are compulsory, as in every Chinese pool, and nothing is provided.

Chapter VII · continued

Courts, pitches
& gyms nearby

Outdoors: courts and pitches

Basketball 篮球场free
Six courts in all — B zone and the covered C-zone court in the north, G zone to the west, H and I zones in the south, plus the indoor one. Turn up with a ball around 17:00–19:00 and you will be waved into a 半场 game.
Football 足球场8:00–18:00
Three pitches: two inside the northern athletics tracks, and the J-zone pitch in the south — north of the New Century footbridge — which is where students actually play. Hours shift with the seasons.
Tennis 网球场
Twelve outdoor courts in the north-west corner (E zone), reached through the gate facing the Xuanling hall or the one shared with F zone. The indoor 玄陵网球馆 has two courts but needs a card and is mostly for teaching and the university team — and no practising against the wall inside.
The track 田径场free
From 18:00 the 400 m track becomes the social hub of the evening. Football pick-up games are organised in WeChat groups — ask your buddy to add you.
UTSEUS · Baoshan Handbook17
Clubs
Chapter VIII

Clubs
& societies

SHU has 111 student clubs, and they are the single easiest way to meet Chinese students — you turn up, you do a thing together, and the language barrier stops mattering. The full directory, translated into English with every group number, is linked from the contents page.

The catch, and it is a real one: clubs organise on QQ, not WeChat, and the numbers in the directory are QQ group IDs. Creating a QQ account needs a Chinese phone number — so sort your SIM out first (the SIM chapter), or ask a classmate who already has one to sign you up and add you to the group.

What is on offer

Sport & outdoors28 clubs
Basketball, football, tennis, volleyball, badminton, table tennis, ultimate frisbee, skateboarding, roller skating, cycling, climbing. The Chinese & International Student Exchange Association GHA sits in this family too, and is the obvious first door for an exchange student: language partners and mixed events.
Music, arts & performance22 clubs
Street dance, two choirs, an original-songwriting club, musical theatre, hip-hop and rap, plus the e-sports crowd (LoL, Valorant, CS) who count as performers here.
Science, tech & robotics22 clubs
RoboMaster combat robotics (new for 2026), an AI club, open-source and Linux, RC aircraft and FPV drones, mathematical modelling, chemistry, astronomy. If you are here on an engineering exchange, this is your natural habitat.
Culture, languages & hobbies23 clubs
The English Association runs a conversation corner where Chinese students come to practise — an easy way in. Also Japanese, Mandarin and pronunciation clubs, Shanghainese dialect and city walks, calligraphy, seal carving, kite making.
Volunteering & social impact16 clubs
Rural teaching trips, hospital and eldercare visits, environmental work, legal aid, sign language, peer mental-health support.
How to join
Find the club in the directory, note its QQ group number, search that number in QQ and request to join. Most groups accept students without ceremony; some ask a question or two. Term start is when everyone recruits, so the first two weeks are the moment to move.

Phone
Chapter X

Get a
SIM card

Your phone number is your digital identity in China. It is essential for opening a bank account, ordering on Taobao, or registering for bike-sharing apps.

The three options near campus

China Unicom — Jufengyuan Road 中国联通 聚丰园路营业厅recommended→ open in maps
155 Jufengyuan Rd · 5 min walk from west gate · ~9:00–17:30
The closest official store to campus, used to SHU students. Unicom is the simplest operator for foreigners: best compatibility with European/foreign phones.
China Telecom — Jufengyuan Road 中国电信 聚丰园路营业厅→ open in maps
329 Jufengyuan Rd · 10 min walk from west gate · ~8:30–18:00
The cheapest of the three operators. This branch is very convenient as it is located on the same street as China Unicom, just a few minutes walk away. Ideal for comparing.
China Mobile — Jufengyuan Road 中国移动 聚丰园路营业厅→ open in maps
189 Jufengyuan Rd · 15 min walk from west gate · ~9:00–17:30
Small official agency (Dachang M-Zone). Very convenient as it is located on the same street as the Unicom branch.
Budget for a semester: 19 to 59 RMB/month. Ask for prepaid with no contract: 预付费，无合约 — and refuse the 12–24 month contracts they will automatically offer you.
  • Keep the number active all semester: a prepaid number with zero balance is suspended then recycled (~90 days) — and with it goes your access to WeChat Pay and your bank. Do small regular top-ups via Alipay.
  • When leaving: cancel in-store (销号) before leaving. Remember to change your phone number on WeChat and Alipay to your home country number.
UTSEUS tip: come with a Chinese-speaking friend or a UTSEUS buddy — passport registration takes time and the staff in these neighborhood shops rarely speak English.

Money
Chapter XI

Open a
bank account

General information (currency, cards, Alipay/WeChat with foreign cards) is in the AFEC guide. Here: branches around campus. Aim to open your account as soon as you have your SIM card and hotel registration. All ATMs of these 4 major banks have an English interface and accept foreign cards.

The four major banks near campus

Bank of China — Qilianshan Road 中国银行祁连山路支行SHU partner→ open in maps
165 Jufengyuan Rd · 5 min walk from the west gate · ~9:00–17:00
The branch cited in the official SHU international student handbook: they process foreign students all day and the staff is used to passports. By far your best chances.
Game-changing tip (30 min instead of 2 hours): Pre-fill your account application on WeChat to skip the paperwork:
  • When you arrive at the branch, ask the staff for the Account Opening WeChat QR Code.
  • Scan it to open the Mini Program, select the "Foreigner" profile, and upload a photo of your passport.
  • Select the Qilianshan Road branch (祁连山路支行) to fast-track your opening.
China Construction Bank — Jinqiu Road 中国建设银行锦秋路支行→ open in maps
Jinqiu Xintiandi, 809 Jinqiu Rd · 10 min walk · ~9:00–17:00
The closest large bank to the Jinqiu/Nanchen area. Opens accounts for foreign students. Their ATMs accept foreign Visa/Mastercard.
ICBC — Jufengyuan Road 中国工商银行聚丰园路支行→ open in maps
458 Jufengyuan Rd · 15 min walk from the west gate · ~9:00–17:00
Very close to the west gate. Excellent alternative if Bank of China is too busy.
Agricultural Bank of China — Jinqiu Road 中国农业银行（锦秋路716号）→ open in maps
716 Jinqiu Rd · 20 min walk from the west gate · ~9:00–17:00
Small neighborhood branch, also walking distance — but small branches sometimes send foreigners to a larger main branch.

Documents to bring — all of them, every time

  • Passport + visa page (and a photocopy of each)
  • SHU Admission Letter
  • Residence Registration Form 临时住宿登记单 (must be requested at your hotel reception; if you are in an apartment, you must register online here)
  • Active Chinese phone number — mandatory, everything is verified via SMS
  • ~100 RMB in cash to activate the card (issuance fee 0–20 RMB)

At the counter, if asked why: 校园卡充值 (top up campus card), reimbursements, and daily expenses. Keep it simple, study-related.

Why a Chinese bank account is useful: While linking a foreign card to Alipay/WeChat (Plan B in the AFEC guide) covers daily life in Baoshan with 0% fees up to 200 RMB per transaction, its real limit is that it is impossible to receive money — hongbao, your flat deposit coming back, or transfers from a friend. This is the main reason to get a Chinese account; once you have it, link it immediately to Alipay and WeChat.
End of semester: empty or close the account before going home (passport + card at any branch of the bank) — a dormant account is a hassle to manage from abroad.

Food
Chapter XII

Eating around
campus

Baoshan is not a trendy neighbourhood — which is good news: everything is student-priced. Three streets to know, a full meal for 15–35 RMB, and a group dinner for 80–130 RMB a head.

The three streets that matter

The west gate 弘基广场15–40 RMB→ open in maps
West exit of campus, Nanchen Rd / Shangda Rd side · 5–10 min walk
Maps call it « Hongji Plaza », but every intake just calls it « the west gate ». Open 24/7, facing New Century. THE food street for SHU students: malatang, chuanchuan skewers (the 鸿基歪串串 stall is a classic), Korean tteokbokki hotpot, stone-bowl bibimbap, fried snacks and a row of bubble tea shops. Stalls change every semester: follow the queues, they are the real guide. Busiest 17:30–21:00.
Jufengyuan Road 聚丰园路20–70 RMB→ open in maps
West side of campus · 10–15 min walk, 2 min by bike
The most complete street: home-style Chinese, Korean, Japanese, hotpot, barbecue, KTV and a cinema. The default answer to « shall we go out for dinner? », with places that stay open late.
The habit to build: open Dianping on 聚丰园路, sort by rating, and buy the 团购 set menu (20–30 % off) before you sit down.
Jinqiu Road 锦秋路20–35 RMB→ open in maps
North side of campus, on foot
A neighbourhood street with a supermarket, fruit shops and the malatang 汆悦麻辣烫: you fill your own bowl (vegetables, tofu, noodles, meats), pay by weight and choose the broth and spice level. The most vegetarian-friendly format in China.
Micheng T3 street 芈城T3科创街south gate→ open in maps
Opposite the south gate, the closest to the teaching buildings
Restaurants, cafés, bubble tea and entertainment: the quickest option when you come out of class and don't want to cross the whole campus to the west gate.

The classics worth knowing

Lanzhou halal noodles 兰州拉面 · 清真
Several shops in the gate streets · 15–22 RMB
Hand-pulled beef noodles, green signs, halal (清真), fast and open late. On campus, floor 3 of the 山明 canteen is dedicated to north-western flavours (the canteens chapter).
Shaxian Snacks 沙县小吃
In the gate streets · meal under 20 RMB
The national budget chain. The classic combo: peanut-sauce noodles plus wonton soup (拌面 + 扁肉) for about 13 RMB.
Bubble tea everywhere 蜜雪冰城 · 一点点 · 霸王茶姬
Hongji, Jufengyuan Rd, the malls · 4–22 RMB
Mixue (red snowman logo) is rock-bottom cheap, Yidiandian the student classic, Chagee the smarter version. Vocabulary: 少糖 less sugar, 去冰 no ice, 珍珠 tapioca pearls.
Late-night skewers 烧烤
Gate streets, 21:00–01:00 · 25–40 RMB a round
Post-library shaokao: lamb, chicken wings, tofu and enoki mushrooms over charcoal. A big bottle of local beer is 8–12 RMB. Saying 撸串 (lū chuàn) will amuse your Chinese classmates.
UTSEUS · Baoshan Handbook24
Food
Chapter XII · continued

Group dinners
& delivery

For a proper dinner together

Haidilao 海底捞火锅100–140 RMB→ open in maps
Branches in Baoshan malls, Line 7 plus a walk or a 20–30 RMB Didi
China's most famous hotpot chain and the ideal first group dinner: legendary service, picture-and-English menu on a tablet. Ask for 鸳鸯锅 (yuānyāng guō), the half-spicy half-mild pot. Book through the app or arrive before 17:30 at weekends — otherwise expect an hour's queue. There is a student discount at certain hours: ask, with your SHU card.
Korean BBQ 韩式烤肉60–100 RMB
Jufengyuan Rd and the nearby malls
Grill-at-the-table, very popular with SHU students. 自助 on a sign means all-you-can-eat (70–100 RMB) — buy the Dianping deal before you sit down.
Jingwei Hui 经纬汇 & Baoshan Life Hub 宝山日月光→ open in maps
Nanchen Rd metro (next station) / Dachang Town · Line 7
Chain restaurants for when the gate streets get repetitive: hotpot, ramen, Cantonese, coffee. Food court 25–45 RMB, sit-down 50–90 RMB. The Life Hub is the livelier of the two.

Delivery, campus edition

Meituan and Eleme (both covered in the AFEC guide) deliver to campus in 30–45 minutes for 2–5 RMB. The SHU specificity: couriers cannot enter the campus — collect your bag from the delivery shelves (外卖架) at the nearest gate and watch for the courier's message. Find your shelf on your very first order.

Searches worth saving once and for all: 麻辣烫 malatang · 饺子 dumplings · 兰州拉面 halal noodles · 奶茶 bubble tea · 清真 halal · 素 vegetarian · 汉堡 burger
  • Chinese meal times: lunch 11:30–12:30, dinner 17:30–19:00. Many small places close at 21:00 — after that it is skewers, convenience stores (FamilyMart/Lawson hot counter) and delivery.
  • Vegetarians: learn 我吃素 (wǒ chī sù); at malatang, ask for the clear broth 清汤 — standard broths are usually bone-based.
  • Cash is nearly useless: everything is paid by Alipay/WeChat QR code, even the skewer stall.
UTSEUS tip: the streets (Hongji, Jufengyuan, Jinqiu) are stable, but individual shops turn over every semester. Before crossing town for one specific address, check on Dianping that it still exists.
UTSEUS · Baoshan Handbook25
Night
Chapter XIII

Bars, clubs
& KTV

Let's be honest: Baoshan is not a party district. Around campus you get student bars and KTV; for real clubs, Line 7 runs straight to Jing'an in 30 minutes. The real question is not where to go out — it is how to get home.

Next to campus

Helen's 海伦司小酒馆< 60 RMB a night→ open in maps
2F Hongji Plaza, 55 Jufengyuan Rd · walking distance from campus
China's national student bar chain: dim lights, dice games, beers at 9.9–15 RMB, pitchers 30–50 RMB. Every SHU student's « first beer in China », and the easiest place to meet Chinese students your own age. The chain has closed branches since 2023: check on Gaode (海伦司) before heading over.
Hongji Plaza bars and taprooms 聚丰园路 · 精酿to be confirmed
Jufengyuan Rd, west side · craft beer 25–45 RMB
A few craft-beer micro-bars and late-opening barbecue counters — all the « nightlife » Baoshan offers on foot. Small places open and close fast: search 精酿 (craft beer) or 酒吧 (bar) around 上海大学站 on Dianping.
KTV — the rite of passage 纯K · 魅KTV · 星聚会
Baoshan and along Line 7 · from 40–80 RMB a room in the afternoon
THE Chinese group night out: private room, touchscreen catalogue (with international songs), drinks brought to your door. Friday prime time runs about 298 RMB for three hours for the room — split six ways, it's nothing. Always book the 团购 deal on Meituan: the walk-in price can be double.

Downtown — direct on Line 7

Wuding Lu / Yanping Lu 武定路 · 延平路Changping Rd · direct
~35 min, no transfer · beers 40–60 RMB, cocktails 60–90 RMB
The nearest proper bar neighbourhood to Baoshan: taprooms, cocktail bars, bistros. Ideal on a weeknight — leave at 23:00 and you still catch the last metro.
Found 158 158坊 — TAXX & 44KWJing'an Temple · direct
158 Julu Lu, ~45 min door to door · entry 0–300 RMB depending on the night and the promoter
TAXX: the EDM/hip-hop mega-club every exchange student does once — and groups of international students very often get in free through WeChat promoters. 44KW: the most stylish club in town, techno and house across two rooms, for people who come for the music. The sunken plaza itself has declined since 2022: go for those two clubs, not for the courtyard atmosphere.
UTSEUS · Baoshan Handbook26
Night
Chapter XIII · continued

Mega-clubs, good deals
& the last metro

INS Park INS新乐园 · 复兴公园168–288 RMB all in
Fuxing Park, ~1 h away · one pass for 7 clubs, one free drink in each
Six floors, seven clubs under one roof: one ticket and you move from room to room all night (free-flow drinks at FRiENDS on the 5th). The most efficient « let's try everything » night in Shanghai — perfect for a group on a Friday.
MASTER TX淮海 5F
~55 min · entry 100–300 RMB
Reputedly Shanghai's biggest club (~4,000 people), with LED visuals designed by teamLab. Worth seeing once, even if EDM isn't your thing.
Perry's
Former French Concession · buckets 30–60 RMB
The legendary cheap student bar: long shared tables, 10 RMB shots, an international crowd. The classic warm-up before a club. Bottom-shelf spirits: eat first, pace yourself.
Elevator 电梯俱乐部
Xujiahui · entry 60–100 RMB
The gateway to the underground scene: a small, relaxed techno club with no bottle-service nonsense. The scene moves fast (ALL Club closed in 2025): follow SmartShanghai for what's on.
Wednesday = ladies' night 女士之夜
Bars in Jing'an and the Concession
A long-running Shanghai tradition: free entry and free drinks for women for part of the night. The venues rotate every season — SmartShanghai keeps the current list. Basic rule: keep an eye on your drink.

Getting back to Baoshan — the real final boss

  • The last metro: what matters is the last Line 7 train towards Meilan Lake 美兰湖方向 — around 23:00–23:15 from Jing'an Temple Sunday to Thursday, extended to about 00:30 on Friday and Saturday. Check in the Metro 大都会 app or Gaode.
  • Missed it: a Didi from downtown to campus takes 30–45 minutes at night and costs 60–100 RMB. Split four ways that's 20 RMB each — always go home as a group.
  • Or the opposite: clubs peak between midnight and 3:00 — plenty of people stay until the first metro (~5:30–6:00), with a noodle or McDonald's stop in between.
  • ID: carry your passport (or a photo of it plus your student card) — big clubs sometimes check, and as a foreigner you should be able to identify yourself if the police do.
  • Your building: living in a flat means no curfew — but check whether your compound locks its gate at night, and make sure you can get in before your first big night out, not at 2 a.m.
The promoter system: big clubs recruit groups of international students through WeChat — free entry, sometimes a free table and drinks. Ask older students to add you to those groups in your first week. There is no obligation to buy anything; be sensible about free-flow alcohol quality.

Chapter XIV

Gyms & classes
around the campus

Gyms around campus

LeFit 乐刻运动129–199 RMB/month→ open in maps
24-hour pods around Dachang and Dahua · search 乐刻 on Gaode
The 24-hour budget chain, ideal for one semester: no contract, pay monthly in the app, QR-code entry at any hour. Single sessions cost 20–40 RMB through Meituan if you want to try first.

Fitness
Chapter XIV · continued

Public pool, climbing
& long runs

Dachang Sports Center 大场体育中心→ open in maps
2010 Hutai Rd · Line 7 → Xingzhi Rd, then 800 m
The district's public complex: heated indoor pool (~30–50 RMB, ~20–30 concession), badminton (30–60 RMB/h), squash, table tennis, billiards, outdoor fitness trail. A solid plan B when campus courts are full — and one of the few squash options around. Pool slots are booked by name through the 上海体育 WeChat account or the 随申办 app; weekend evenings go three days ahead.
Gucun Park 顾村公园~20 RMB→ open in maps
Line 7 towards Meilan Lake → Gucun Park (~10 min), exit 5
Shanghai's largest suburban forest park and the best long-run terrain near campus: kilometres of shaded paths around a lake, with bikes for rent. In spring it hosts the famous cherry blossom festival (16,000 trees, enormous crowds); the rest of the year it is quiet. Open 6:00–18:00.
Beta Boulders 难点攀岩馆Changping Rd · direct→ open in maps
667 Changhua Rd, Jing'an · ~30–35 min on Line 7 · entry 100–150 RMB plus 10–20 for shoes
The serious bouldering gym that is easiest to reach from SHU — straight down your own metro line. Modern walls, a Kilter board, a very international and English-speaking crowd, and beginners welcome with no certification. Ten-visit punch cards bring the price down; WeChat: beta-boulders-gym.
SuperMonkey 超级猩猩→ open in maps
Daning / Jing'an, Line 7 towards the centre · 69–159 RMB per class
Pay-per-class group fitness with no membership: HIIT, boxing, spinning, dance, yoga — booked in the WeChat mini-program. For cheaper yoga closer to campus, search 瑜伽 on Dianping around Dahua: trial classes go for 19–39 RMB on Meituan.

Worth knowing

  • Counter vocabulary: 预约 book · 场地 court · 羽毛球 badminton · 游泳馆 pool · 健身房 gym · 月卡 monthly pass · 次卡 punch card.
  • Pools: swim caps are compulsory everywhere (15 RMB on Taobao); deep-water zones sometimes require a 深水证 or a short swim test — otherwise stay in the standard lanes.
  • Running: download Keep (the Chinese Strava, with an English mode). August and September are brutally humid — locals run after 19:00. Check the AQI before hard outdoor sessions.
  • Beware of memberships: the big traditional chains (Will's and others) have been closing clubs since 2024 and prepaid cards are hard to refund. Monthly or pay-per-class, never annual.

Chapter XV

Shopping &
daily life

Everything is either walking distance or one metro stop away, everything is cheaper than downtown — and whatever is missing arrives at your door within a day or two via Taobao.

Groceries

Campus supermarkets 校内超市
Next to the dorms and canteens
Your first stop on day one: water (2 RMB), instant noodles, toiletries, hangers, a bucket, a power strip. Subsidised prices, often cheaper than outside.
Lianhua 联华超市（锦秋店）→ open in maps
Jinqiu Rd, 10–15 min walk
The proper neighbourhood supermarket: vegetables, eggs, cleaning products. Basic and complete — a week's shopping runs 50–150 RMB.
Sam's Club 山姆会员商店5 min walk→ open in maps
Leave New Century 新世纪大学生村, turn left, five minutes — it's on your right
The biggest supermarket near campus and bulk-shopping heaven: imported food, cheese, meat, XXL portions. Share one membership card between friends, like at METRO.
Hema / Freshippo 盒马
Delivery in 30–60 min through the app
Good fruit, ready meals, some imported goods — order in the app rather than trekking to a store (the nearest are in Dahua). The old Hema X membership store in Dachang closed in 2025: ignore older blog posts.
METRO at the Life Hub 麦德龙会员店→ open in maps
B1 Baoshan Life Hub · membership ~199 RMB/year
Cheese, charcuterie, wine, European products — the official cure for homesickness. Share a membership card between classmates, Costco-style.

The malls

Baoshan Life Hub 宝山日月光中心Dachang Town · Line 7→ open in maps
Direct access from metro exit 1 · Line 7
THE mall for SHU students: 175,000 m² of restaurants, a cinema (40–60 RMB through Meituan), karting, a trampoline park, fashion chains, MINISO and the METRO store downstairs.
Jingwei Hui 经纬汇 Nanchen Rd  ·  Wanda Plaza 宝山万达→ open in maps
Jingwei Hui, right across from campus: handy for a quick dinner, but half-empty — keep expectations low. Wanda is on Line 1 (Gongkang Rd), a 25–35 RMB taxi away: only worth it if you are already nearby.

Practical
Chapter XV · continued

Pharmacies, deliveries
& small services

Pharmacies 药房
24/7: 378 Hanqing Rd to be confirmed · chains around Jinqiu Rd
Most basics are available without a prescription. Show the Chinese name: ibuprofen 布洛芬 (Fenbid 芬必得) · paracetamol 泰诺 · cold medicine 999感冒灵 · plasters 创可贴 · antihistamine 氯雷他定. Sick at 2 a.m.? Meituan delivers from pharmacies in 30 minutes.
Cainiao parcel station 菜鸟驿站→ open in maps
Lane 1288 Shangda Rd, no. 44 · ~3,000 parcels a day
Every Taobao/Pinduoduo/JD parcel lands here: you get a pickup code by SMS or in the 菜鸟 app. Set your Taobao address as 上海市宝山区南陈路333号上海大学 plus your building, name and Chinese number.
Bedding & day-one kit
Taobao (48 h) · MINISO at the Life Hub · the 2-yuan bazaars on Jinqiu Rd
Furnished flats rarely come with bedding. Search 四件套 (four-piece bedding set, 60–150 RMB) once you know your mattress size — 1.5米床 for a double, 0.9米床 for a single. A duvet costs 50–120 RMB.
Print shops 打印店 & barbers 理发店
Around the gates and lane 1288 Shangda Rd
Printing: send your PDF to the shop's WeChat (B&W 0.1–0.5 RMB a page, 黑白 black and white, 双面 double-sided). A student haircut costs 15–35 RMB: say 只要剪发 (« just a cut ») and firmly decline the loyalty card (不用了, búyòng le).

Convenience stores, fruit & bikes

  • FamilyMart 全家 / Lawson 罗森 are everywhere, many open 24/7: onigiri 5–8 RMB, bento 12–20 RMB, hot counter (oden 关东煮, baozi) — the official late-night student meal.
  • Fruit is far cheaper than at home, and sold by the 斤 (jin = 500 g, not the kilo!): bananas 3–5, apples 5–8, seasonal mango or lychee 10–20 RMB per jin.
  • Shared bikes (HelloBike through Alipay, Meituan): the way to cross this enormous campus and reach the metro. About 1.5–2 RMB a ride; buy the monthly pass 骑行月卡 (~15–17 RMB) in your first week — it pays for itself in ten rides. Park inside the painted zones or you'll be fined.
UTSEUS tip: on arrival day buy only the essentials at the campus supermarket, then order everything else on Taobao as soon as your SIM works — cheaper than any shop, and at your door in one to three days.

Explore
Chapter XVI

Line 7,
your lifeline

It stops at the campus gate and runs straight to Jing'an with no transfer: 28 minutes, 4–5 RMB. Everything this guide recommends downtown is on this diagram.

What's at the other end, ranked from Baoshan

Jing'an Temple 静安寺direct · 28 min→ open in maps
The golden temple surrounded by towers — your default « let's go into town » stop, with no transfer. The temple costs 50 RMB, the park and malls are free. It is also the platform where you catch the last train home.
M50 & Suzhou Creek M50创意园free~35 min→ open in maps
140 art galleries in a former textile mill — the genuinely cool place closest to Baoshan (Changshou Rd then L13, or a walk from Zhenping Rd). Carry on along the renovated Suzhou Creek promenade to the Sihang warehouse 四行仓库. Many galleries close on Mondays.
Former French Concession & Wukang Road 武康路Changshu Rd · direct→ open in maps
Plane trees, 1920s villas and the Wukang Building. Get off at Changshu Rd, grab a bike and ride Wukang → Anfu → Fuxing. A weekday afternoon is far better than a weekend.
The Bund 外滩free→ open in maps
Jing'an then Line 2 to East Nanjing Rd (~45–50 min). The lights go off at 23:00 sharp — by then your last metro has gone, so a Bund evening means a shared Didi. The insider move: the 2 RMB Shiliupu ferry, the cheapest river cruise in Shanghai.
Wujiaochang & Daxue Road 五角场 · 大学路Didi ~40–50 RMB→ open in maps
The Fudan/Tongji student quarter: terraces, beers at 15–35 RMB, student prices throughout. Awkward by metro from Baoshan but close as the crow flies — the one case where a shared Didi beats the train.
UTSEUS tip: go out in groups (the Didi home drops from 80 to 20 RMB a head), always carry your passport, and get into the habit of pasting this guide's Chinese names into Gaode. For trips beyond Shanghai (Suzhou, Hangzhou…), see the AFEC guide — trains, tickets and tips are covered there.

SOS
Chapter XVII

If something
goes wrong

The last page, so you can find it by flipping to the back. Save the three numbers in your phone now, before you need them.

Emergency numbers

110
Police
120
Ambulance (chargeable)
119
Fire brigade

Operators rarely speak English. If you can, hand the phone to a Chinese speaker — or send your location in WeChat to someone who can call for you.

Ill rather than in danger

For everyday things — a cold, a sprain, a prescription — start at the campus clinic 校医院 at the north gate. It is also the only route to being reimbursed: the referral rules are in the clinic chapter. Out of hours, Meituan delivers from pharmacies in about 30 minutes (the daily-life chapter).

Something serious

Shanghai General Hospital — International Medical Care Center 上海市第一人民医院国际医疗保健中心→ open in maps
86 Wujin Road, Hongkou · floors 6, 9 and 10 · open 24 hours
This is where to go when it is beyond a campus-clinic problem: a fracture, a fever that will not break, anything needing a scan, anything frightening. It is the international wing of a major public hospital, staffed in English (also Japanese and Russian), so you can describe your symptoms properly instead of miming them — which is the whole difference when something is actually wrong.
24-hour assistance: +86 21 6324 3852 · +86 21 6324 0090 ext. 6413 · imcc@shgh.cn. It is in Hongkou, the district just south of Baoshan — 30 to 40 minutes by Didi from campus, and the closest English-speaking hospital care you have.
There is a second branch in the south of the city, at 650 Xin Song Jiang Road (24 h: +86 21 3779 8630), but from Baoshan the Wujin Road one is the one you want.
Two things to know before you need it: an international centre bills more than a normal Chinese ward, so keep every receipt and check what your insurance covers — and going straight there rather than through the campus clinic may cost you the university reimbursement. When it is serious, go anyway: sort the paperwork out afterwards, and tell Charly.

Consulate

Consulate General of France in Shanghai — Soho Zhongshan Plaza, 1055 West Zhongshan Road, building A, 18th floor. Consular emergencies: +86 21 6103 2200. Students of other nationalities: look up your own consulate in Shanghai before you travel.

And in any case, tell someone from the team. Charly for visas and SHU registration, Kay and Anicet for housing, Kay for academic trouble, Anicet for everything else — and Fabien if it is serious. All four are in Chapter I. You are not expected to sort out a problem in a foreign country on your own.
Have a great semester! Written by Anicet Barrios, Head Student Coordinator at UTSEUS. Corrections and new addresses are very welcome — on WeChat, obviously.
